  A.  Commission Assignments
  Recommended Action:  1) Review the Parks and Recreation Commission
  assignments for Fiscal Year 2023-24; and 2) Recommend assignments for Fiscal
  Year 2024-25 for City Council consideration.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  Commissioner Skophammer requested that the assignments be renumbered by
  priority. He suggested revising Assignment 1 to state, "Review and provide
  feedback regarding the Permanent Skate Park permitting and fundraising efforts."
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of April I 6, 2024
  Page 3 of7

Commissioner Lingo suggested revising Assignment 2 to state, "Provide feedback
and recommendations to the City Council regarding the design of the permanent
snack shack, related facilities, and landscaping."

Commissioner Peak suggested adding an assignment, "Provide feedback regarding
the Malibu Community Lands Outreach survey results." She stated the assignment
should be priority number 3.

Community Services Director Riesgo suggested revising Assignment 4 to state,
"Receive updates and provide feedback on the Legacy Park Rehabilitation Project."
She stated the project was ongoing, and staff would have park updates at
Commission meetings.

Commissioner Peak suggested removing Assignment 6 regarding park tours. She
stated park tours were unnecessary annually and the Commission should visit parks
every two years.

Commissioner Goldfarb requested Assignment I 6, "Provide recommendations to
the City Council regarding the removal of invasive species to decrease fire risk,"
be moved to Assignment 5.

Commissioner Peak suggested adding, "Review and provide feedback regarding a
permanent softball field at a city facility."

Commissioner Lingo indicated agreement with Commissioner Peak.

Community Services Director Riesgo stated a revision to "Nominate and
recommend recipient(s) for the 2025 Jake Kuredjian Citizenship Award to City
Council."

Community Services Director Riesgo stated that Assignment I l and Assignment 4
could be combined and revised to "Receive updates and provide feedback on the
Legacy Park Rehabilitation Project and outdoor programming relating to
rehabilitation or integration of native habitats."

Commissioner Peak suggested revising and separating Assignment I 4 to "Review
and provide feedback and recommendations for the Cham1lee Nature Center
reopening" and "Review and provide feedback on mentorship and docent programs
to incorporate community leaders, retired professionals, athletes, business owners,
or college students at City parks."

Commissioner Skophammer stated Assignment 8 should be the Charmlee Nature
Center.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting

  Community Services Director Riesgo suggested removing Assignment 10,
  "Review the Department's program offerings and make recommendations, as
  appropriate, including the incorporation of various programs at local schools,"
  because Assignment 17, "Review and provide feedback regarding monthly staff
  updates on parks, programs, facilities, and projects" was similar and encompassed
  everything in a simplified version.

  Commissioner Lingo inquired about Assignment 18 regarding potential uses for the
  Malibu Equestrian Park.

  Community Services Director Riesgo stated that the city maintained the Malibu
  Equestrian Park, but the Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School District owned the
  property.

  In response to Commissioner Lingo, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  that an item to discuss programming and review maintenance costs for the
  Equestrian Park would be added to a future agenda.

  Community Lands Outreach survey results;" 4) prioritize the feedback regarding
  the Malibu Community Lands Outreach survey results assignment as Assignment

  Legacy Park Rehabilitation Project and outdoor programming relating to
  rehabilitation or integration of native habitats;" 5) prioritize Assignment 16 to
  Assignment 5; 6) add an assignment to "Review and provide feedback regarding a
  permanent softball field at a city facility;" 7) revise Assignment 9 to "Nominate
  and recommend recipient(s) for the 2025 Jake Kuredjian Citizenship Award to City
  Council;" 8) revise Assignment 14 to "Review and provide feedback and
  recommendations for the Charmlee Nature Center reopening;" 9) prioritize the
  Charmee Nature Center reopening assignment to Assignment 8; 10) revise
  assignment 14 to "Review and provide feedback on mentorship and docent
  programs to incorporate community leaders, retired professionals, athletes,
  business owners, or college students at City parks;" 10) remove Assignment 6, 10,
  and 11. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0; Vice Chair Guldimann
  absent.

  B.  Program Proposal for Recreation Programs
  Recommended Action: 1) Review the Request for Qualifications criteria for
  recreation program proposals; and 2) Provide feedback to staff.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of April 16, 2024
  Page 5 of7

  Recreation Manager Manisco presented the staff report.

  Commissioner Skophammer suggested modifying the Agreement to a two-year
  term with the option to extend yearly for three additional years.

  Commissioner Lingo agreed with the staff recommended three-year term, which
  would allow instructors time to build community relationships and establish their
  program.

  Commissioner Goldfarb stated that the contract instructor should be monitored, and
  participants should evaluate the program.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Recreation Manager Manisco stated that an
  online Program Feedback Survey and Program Interest Survey were available on
  the City's website and could be completed anytime.

  In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Recreation Manager Manisco stated
  agency professionals would review the proposals, and City staff would evaluate the
  feedback to select a contractor.

MOTION  Commissioner Peak moved, and Commissioner Skophammer seconded a motion
  to approve the Request for Qualifications criteria for recreation program proposals.
  The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0; Vice Chair Guldimann absent.

  C.  Jake Kurediian Citizenship Award
  Recommended Action: Discuss the nomination process for the 2024 Jake
  Kuredjian Citizenship Award.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  Commissioner Skophammer suggested opening a public nomination period.

  Commissioner Peak nominated Shari Latta. She stated Ms. Latta was the Director
  of Children's Creative Workshop, a former lifeguard for the Los Angeles County
  Fire Department, and was involved in the Malibu community.

  Commissioner Skophammer indicated agreement with Commissioner Peak. He
  nominated John Mills, who was instrumental in creating the LA Westside Bruins
  youth football league and was involved in various sports programs.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Community Services Director Riesgo stated the
  public nomination period would be open for six weeks. She stated staff would
  contact youth sports organizations about the award and nomination period.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of April 16, 2024
  Page 6 of7

  Commissioner Goldfarb nominated Poison Free Malibu for their environmental
  contribution.

  In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated the Jake Kuredj ian Citizenship Award recognized an outstanding
  individual(s) or group who donated time and resources to enhance the quality of
  parks and recreation programs within the Malibu Community.

  Commissioner Goldfarb stated Poison Free Malibu had helped enhance parks by
  banning the use of pesticides.

CONSENSUS
  By Consensus, the Commission agreed to open the public nomination period for
  the 2024 Jake Kuredjian Citizenship Award.

  D.  Permanent Skate Park Fundraising
  Recommended Action: Review and provide feedback regarding fundraising efforts
  for the Permanent Skate Park.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  In response to Commissioner Lingo, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  the City did not have a naming rights policy and had not determined sponsorship
  opportunities.

  Commissioner Peak stated she wanted to ensure community involvement during
  the fundraising efforts.

  Commissioner Skophammer stated there could be multiple community members
  who would donate funds for the Permanent Skate Park.

  Commissioner Peak stated she did not support corporate sponsorships.

  Commissioner Skophammer stated Council should determine how the City should
  manage fundraising.

CONSENSUS
  By Consensus, the Commission agreed to table Item 5.D. until further direction
  was provided by the City Council.

Subject:  Community Services Department Monthly Report

RECOMMENDED ACTION : Receive and file a report of activities, events, projects , and
programs coordinated by the Community Services Department in May 2024.

DISCUSSION: The Community Services Department coordinated the following activities,
projects, and programs in May 2024.

RECREATION
Aquatics: Learn to Swim lessons concluded on May 18. Twenty-one participants , ages
one through ten , learned swimming techniques and motor skills through weekly classes
instructed by aquatics staff.

Aqua Aerobics concluded on May 18 with thirty participants.

Community Programs: The spring session of community classes ended in May. Offerings
included , ballet, barre fitness, hip-hop dance, Music Together, soccer, skateboarding, tai-
chi , t-ball , and tennis. Parent-and-me , youth, and adult recreation programs had over 120
participants.

A beginner photography workshop took place on May 3 with seven participants. Students
learned photography concepts and practiced taking photos of people and landscapes.

On May 10, The Mindry hosted a Manifestation Meditation workshop for eight attendees
at Malibu Bluffs Park. The workshop included practicing affirmations, deep breathing, and
maintaining a state of mindfulness to cultivate positivity.

  Page 1 of 3  Agenda Item# 3.B.2 .
 A salsa dance workshop occurred on May 20 for fourteen attendees at Malibu Bluffs Park.
Students learned basic salsa steps, rhythm, and timing.

Outdoor Recreation: Staff led a wildflower hike on May 4 for thirteen participants. The
hikers learned about wildflowers and songbirds.

Forty-four participants engaged in the Legacy Park Agents of Discovery application in
May. Participants learned about the City's Earth Friendly· Management Program,
pollinators, and the chaparral ecosystem.

Seniors: Weekly recreation programs continued in the Senior Center and Malibu Bluffs
Park including, art trek, ballet, cardio salsa, chair yoga, choir, knitting, yoga, Pilates,
coloring, stretch and strength, and tap/jazz dance.

On May 6, Meadowbrook Senior Living led a Coffee and Donuts discussion for twelve
seniors. Attendees learned how to prepare for the transition to senior living and the daily
structure of a senior facility.

The Silver Fox Walk at Zuma Beach took place on May 9 with six seniors. The program is
designed to encourage peer engagement and to be active outdoors.

Twenty seniors attended an excursion to SONY Studios on May 21. Attendees took a
guided walking tour of the studio lot, took pictures on the "Jeopardy" set, and enjoyed
lunch in Downtown Culver City.

The monthly luncheon for eighty-six participants took place on May 23. Attendees were
served chicken pesto sandwiches, kale and apple salad, potato salad, and chips. The
event included a performance by the Senior Center Choir, and a raffle for gift certificates
donated by The Mindry for Wellness. The Boys & Girls Club of Malibu provided birdhouses
and wind chimes to celebrate their "Kindness is Free" campaign. Additionally, the Malibu
Community Lands outreach team provided information on the City's engagement plan.

Fifteen participants attended the monthly craft workshop and created pressed flower glass
frames. Seniors selected from various pressed flowers and ribbons to put in a gold glass
frame. Refreshments were also provided.

Social Media: Department social media posts featured summer registration dates, day
camps, parent-and-me programs, senior center programs, and learn-to-swim lessons. In
May 2024, lnstagram reached 1,000 accounts, and Facebook reached 931 accounts.

Special Events: "When I Grow Up" Park Tales took place on May 9 at Malibu Bluffs Park
in partnership with the Malibu Library. Twelve families received an art activity, program
flyers, snacks, and a book donated by the Malibu Library. Special guests included Deputy
Knott from the Lost Hills Sheriff's Department.

  Page 2 of 3  Agenda Item# 3.B,2.
 PARK MAINTENANCE
Charm lee Park: The trail crew from Managed Career Solutions has exceeded expectations
and cleared Priority 1 and conducted weed abatement inside the water tank fenced area.

Upgraded the restroom lighting, including fixtures and wiring, from fluorescent lights to
light-emitting diode (LED) lights.

Las Flores Park: Installed decomposed granite (DG), graded and leveled all park trails,
and added binding material which assists with erosion mitigation.

Legacy Park: Removed over three hundred square feet of nonnative, invasive sweet
clover, tocalote, mustard, and euphorbia as part of the annual maintenance schedule. The
area was hand-weeded by staff.

Pressure-washed all park benches and hardscape surfaces.

Installed decomposed granite (DG), graded and leveled all park trails, and added binding
material which assists with erosion mitigation. The installation and repair work began in
May and will extend through June.

Malibu Bluffs Park: Replaced and installed a chain ladder on the playground near the
Michael Landon Center. The protective rubber coating began to crack, requiring a
replacement.

Tilled the sand in the playground near the Whale Tale outlook to remove foreign materials.

Replaced and installed a new rodent proof door seal around the maintenance building's
garage door in the maintenance yard.

Pressure-washed all park benches and hardscape surfaces.

Serviced and cleaned the irrigation weather station.

Medians and Parkways: Repaired a broken antenna wire for the Treatment Plant irrigation
controller and re-established Wi-Fi connection.

Michael Landon Center: Replaced two smoke alarms and installed four new smoke alarms
in the Michael Landon Center.

Trancas Canyon Park: Completed annual weed abatement on all perimeter slopes.

Trancas Field Open Space: Staff deadheaded hundreds of Castor Bean plants and
removed over two hundred seedlings and large Castor Bean plants.

Subject:  Jake Kuredjian Citizenship Award

RECOMMENDED ACTION: 1) Review and discuss the nominations for the 2024 Jake
Kuredjian Citizenship Award; and 2) Select a nominee for City Council consideration.

DISCUSSION: At the recommendation of the Parks and Recreation Commission, the City
Council created the Jake Kuredjian Citizenship Award in 2002 to recognize an outstanding
individual(s) or group who donated time and resources to enhance the quality of parks and
recreation programs within the Malibu community.

The award was created to honor Los Angeles County Sherriff's Deputy Hagop "Jake"
Kuredjian, who was killed in the line of duty on August 31 , 2001, after 17 years of service.
Deputy Kuredjian was presented the Gold Meritorious Conduct Medal in 1989 for rescuing
a woman from a cliff in Malibu.

Past recipients of the Jake Kuredjian Citizenship Award have demonstrated a commitment
to and involvement in recreation in Malibu and, in doing so, demonstrated the highest level
of citizenship while making a lasting contribution to the community.

At the April 16, 2024 Regular meeting , the Commission discussed the nomination process
and, by consensus, determined to open nominations to the public. The City publicized the
open nomination period on the City's website, social media channels, and in the Malibu
Times . Additionally, staff contacted local organizations, including Malibu Little League,
American Youth Soccer Organization (AYSO), Malibu Aquatics Foundation , Malibu
Marlins Swim Club, and the Boys & Girls Club of Malibu. The nomination process resulted
in one nominee, Patt Healy (Attachment 1):

  Page 1 of 2  Agenda Item # 4 .A.
 Commissioner Peak recommended former County of LA Fire Department Lifeguard and
Children's Creative Workshop Director Shari Latta. Commissioner Skophammer
recommended John Mills, who was known as the founder of the LA Westside Bruins
football. Commissioner Goldfarb recommended Poison Free Malibu for their
environmental advocacy.

The Commission is asked .to review and discuss the nominee and Commissioner
recommendations for the 2024 Jake Kuredjian Citizenship Award. The Commission may
select an individual(s) or group from or select a different individual(s) or group not included
in the public nomination process. The nominee(s) would be required to meet the
recognition criteria and could be approved by a majority vote, then provided to City Council
for consideration.

Subject:  Malibu Equestrian Park

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file a report regarding programming and the
operation of the Malibu Equestrian Park.

DISCUSSION: The City entered a Recreation Agreement (Agreement) with Santa Monica
Malibu Unified School District (SMMUSD) to operate and maintain the Malibu Equestrian
Park for 25 years in 1995. In 2008 , the City discovered no one had a signed copy of the
1995 Agreement, and the Council approved the continuance of the Agreement through
2022 (Attachment 1). In 2023, the City and SMMUSD discussed Section 6 - Terms of the
Agreement and determined that the term would continue yearly until both parties agree to
terminate the Agreement.

As part of the Agreement, the City must complete and pay the related fees for park
maintenance. The City opens the Malibu Equestrian Park seven days a week from 8:00
AM to sunset, 365 days a year. The City's Park Division oversees and completes weed
abatement, daily maintenance, landscape maintenance, restroom maintenance, stocking
paper goods, and arena upkeep. Maintaining the Malibu Equestrian Park costs
approximately $81 ,000 annually (Attachment 2).

The City and Trancas Riders and Ropers (TR&R), a local nonprofit organization , had a
community use agreement for several years. The agreement's primary objective was to
allow the group to reserve space for programs and events, as well as provide the City with
feedback and assistance with maintenance and upkeep. TR&R remained active through
2018 but disbanded following the Woolsey Fire.

The Community Services Department has attempted to schedule programs at the
Equestrian Park, but this has been somewhat difficult due to insurance requirements and
instructor liability. Staff plans to review options to reinstate programming in Fiscal Year

  Page 1 of 2  Agenda Item# 5.A .
 2024-25 through the City's RFQ process.  Programming options may include riding
lessons or equine therapy.
